# Optical counterpart at SN 2019wqq

The optical position in the Transient Name Server lies 0.13 arcseconds from SDSS J103504.84+463338.1, an object cataloged a decade before the supernova. The VLASS epoch-three centroid is 0.37 arcseconds from that optical object. Richards et al. (2009) retained it as a photometric quasar candidate with quality flag 0 on a scale from −6 to +6, prior classification U (unknown), no measured redshift, no tabulated radio counterpart, and photometric errors of 0.46–0.75 mag in g, r, i and z. The reported 0.910 is the photometric probability of the redshift interval 0.910–1.400 conditional on their model, not a probability that the object is a quasar. Their modal photometric redshift is 1.115.

Gaia DR3 source 830717048086240000 is 0.39 arcseconds from the SDSS position. Its DSC combined-model probabilities favor a galaxy (0.9753) over a quasar (0.00857). There is no Gaia parallax or proper motion solution for this source. Its BP/RP measurement in the bright central light of UGC 5744 may mix components. The pre-explosion Pan-STARRS1 g/r/i stack, centered on the Richards position with north up and east left, shows compact structure superposed on the bright galaxy light. The image does not distinguish a cluster, H II region, or background source. The cutout measures 60 arcseconds on a side.

The sole SDSS spectrum within 15 arcseconds has its fiber centered on the galaxy, 3.08 arcseconds from the candidate (MJD 52615, plate 961, fiber 77, STARFORMING GALAXY, redshift 0.01119638, ZWARNING 0). The nearest DESI DR1 main/bright spectrum, 3.58 arcseconds away, also belongs to the galaxy (TARGETID 39633191329334637, redshift 0.01116280, ZWARN 0). We queried the redrock files for HEALPix 5902 in the published main, sv1, sv2, sv3, and special bright/dark directories. The main/bright file existed. The nine other file locations returned HTTP 404. Neither of the two measured host redshifts establishes the identity of the coincident optical point source. The progenitor association of the radio emission remains ambiguous.

The JSON contains compact catalog rows, spherical small-angle offsets, queries and product URLs. The JPEG is the unaltered STScI color cutout from the pre-2019 survey.
